        16       391, by Senator Saland, Senate Print 2379-A,

        17       an act to amend the Criminal Procedure Law,

        18       the Executive Law, the Family Court Act and

        19       the Penal Law.

        20                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

        21       Paterson, did you ask for an explanation?

        24                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

        25       Saland, an explanation of Calendar Number 391







                                                          1869

         1       has been requested by Senator Paterson.

         2                      SENATOR SALAND:  Thank you, Mr.

         3       President.

         4                      Mr. President, this is the

         5       Juvenile Justice Accountability and Procedural

         6       Reform Act of 1998.  It mirrors a similar

         7       Governor's program bill that this house passed

         8       last year.  It's an effort to deal in a

         9       comprehensive fashion with the ever

        10       troublesome and certainly extraordinarily

        11       difficult issue of juvenile crime; but what

        12       this bill endeavors to do is to create an

        13       approach by which we deal with violent youths

        14       in a fashion which, far too frequently,

        15       appears to be a situation in which gratuitous

        16       and violent crime well beyond the national

        17       statistics, seems to be occurring here in the

        18       state of New York, and what we endeavor to do

        19       is to deal with violent crime.  We endeavor to

        20       impose steeper sentences not merely in the

        21       case of juvenile offenders in our criminal

        22       courts, but also juvenile delinquents by way

        23       of increased penalties to designated felonies

        24       in our Family Courts, but at the same time we

        25       look to a host of other avenues with which to







                                                          1870

         1       deal with alternatives.  We create an

         2       alternatives commission, the purpose of which

         3       is to try and find the optimum and the best of

         4       alternative programs by which to divert young

         5       people into, hopefully, lives that will not

         6       take them down the path of crime but lives of

         7       opportunity.

         8                      We look to such new creations

         9       as the dispositional services plan, to have

        10       greater court involvement in assuring that

        11       these young people will not merely have

        12       services but that there will be court follow

        13       up because I believe most people are aware or

        14       certainly should be aware of the fact that

        15       what occurs today in a system that basically

        16       goes back some 30 or 40 years, there were some

        17       amendments back I believe in early -- the

        18       early 1980s, but it's basically a system that

        19       was conceived to deal with a different type of

        20       a juvenile, a juvenile that wasn't given to

        21       gun possession, that wasn't given to violent

        22       crime, a juvenile that wasn't involved heavily

        23       in the use of or trafficking in drugs.  We're

        24       talking about a system that was conceived to

        25       deal with juveniles that dealt with things







                                                          1871

         1       such as car theft, joy rides, perhaps petit

         2       larceny, nothing of the enormous magnitude

         3       that we're experiencing today, and certainly

         4       if you were to take a look at the statistics

         5       and go back some ten years you would see

         6       extraordinary increases in the level of

         7       juvenile crime, and while certainly it must be

         8       acknowledged that in the course of the past

         9       couple of years we've seen some diminution in

        10       those numbers, what this bill is about is

        11       really not about those who don't commit crime

        12       but how we should treat those who choose to

        13       commit crime, and we do a number of things

        14       here, and let me just give you a brief

        15       selection of some of the more significant or

        16       salient futures of this bill.

        17                      I alluded earlier to the fact

        18       that we provide for increased sentences for

        19       juvenile offenders who commit violent crime.

        20       Very similarly in a parallel fashion, the same

        21       thing occurs in the Family Court for violent

        22       juvenile delinquents who commit designated

        23       felony offenses.  We take the construct of the

        24       Youthful Offender Law, which I think we all

        25       recognize was intended to ensure that a young







                                                          1872

         1       person who commits an act, perhaps some

         2       misconduct that might even be out of character

         3       or first instance in which he or she is

         4       engaged in misconduct, criminal misconduct,

         5       and that youthful offender says that through

         6       your 17th year we're going to give you the

         7       ability, in effect, not to be tarnished by

         8       that act that you committed, we're going to

         9       give you youthful offender status.

        10                      What this bill says is, we're

        11       still going to give you youthful offender

        12       status.  However, if you haven't learned your

        13       lesson, if in fact you persist in committing

        14       these types of crimes and if you commit a

        15       violent felony, what we're going to do is we

        16       are going -- if you commit that crime within

        17       five years of your receiving a youthful

        18       offender adjudication, we're going to permit

        19       the court to go back and look at that

        20       preceding youthful offender adjudication and

        21       if, in fact, the underlying crime was a felony

        22       you will now find yourself in a predicate

        23       felony situation, which I certainly think

        24       would be appropriate and warranted.

        25                      We're doing things







                                                          1873

         1       procedurally.  What we're doing, among other

         2       things, is we're enabling the Family Court to

         3       be one of the courts that has the ability to

         4       issue search warrants.  We're doing -- what

         5       we're doing also is we're dealing with the

         6       issue of the speedy trial problem where a

         7       young person effectively absconds, disappears,

         8       doesn't appear in court and the presentment

         9       agency finds itself in a situation in which if

        10       they can not show due diligence, that time

        11       runs and they are effectively barred. What

        12       we're saying is the speedy -- that speedy

        13       trial clock is going to be tolled while that

        14       young person chooses to absent themselves from

        15       the jurisdiction of the court or the

        16       proceeding that the court has before it.

        17                      We give victims the opportunity

        18       to have their day in court, so the court can

        19       hear them in the course of making its

        20       disposition or issuing its decision and

        21       order.  Very importantly, the bill talks time

        22       and again about juvenile accountability and

        23       parental support therefor, and what we do is

        24       involve parents.  We want parents to be

        25       involved in this process.  We want parents to







                                                          1874

         1       have the opportunity to deal with the court,

         2       with the agencies that are involved with the

         3       disposition of the case, to try and assist

         4       their children in getting back on the right

         5       track.

         6                      The bill also, as has already

         7       occurred with Judge Kaye's directive, opens

         8       the Family Court.  This would statutorily

         9       accomplish the same thing.  Increased records

        10        -- increased access to juvenile records.  If,

        11       for instance, a young person were to apply for

        12       a job as a police officer, if a young person

        13       was to apply for a gun license, this bill says

        14       that you would have the ability to access

        15       juvenile records that would have otherwise

        16       been sealed, to determine what that person's

        17       background is, and in fact they are

        18       appropriate candidates either for a

        19       police-related job or the ability to carry a

        20       gun.

        21                      I mentioned in my earlier

        22       comments we create an alternatives commission,

        23       a seven-member commission with representatives

        24       from both houses and from the Governor, the

        25       purpose of which is to maximize the kinds of







                                                          1875

         1       alternative placements that we can resort to,

         2       and similarly there's provision in this bill

         3       for the use of something which we have really

         4       attempted to enact into law since 1995, a

         5       dispositional services plan which will enable

         6       much more of a hands-on approach, much greater

         7       control, and also provides for the requirement

         8       of after-care planning by the Office of

         9       Children and Family Services.

        10                      So this bill really represents

        11       the -- the continuing effort of the Senate

        12       Majority working closely with the Governor to

        13       deal with comprehensive juvenile justice

        14       reform.  This is something that we initiated

        15       by the introduction of legislation back in

        16       1995.  This house in 1996 passed a

        17       comprehensive juvenile justice reform bill.

        18       In 1997, we passed after working out an

        19       agreement with the Governor, his Governor's

        20       program bill which is now back in front of us

        21       here in this session, the 1998 session.

        22                      Certainly we welcome however

        23       belatedly, the involvement of the Assembly.

        24       We know that this year, after considerable

        25       talk about doing something about juvenile







                                                          1876

         1       justice, they have in fact passed a measure

         2       and we look forward to the opportunity to find

         3       where we have a common interest and trying to

         4       work towards closure of this issue during this

         5       1998 session.

         6                      A critical issue, an issue of

         7       great importance to all of us in all of our

         8       communities, and I would be very remiss if I

         9       did not mention, as I referred in my earlier

        10       comments, to the fact that the numbers

        11       certainly are staggering when compared to the

        12       numbers of some ten years ago.  The numbers of

        13       crimes that are committed in New York State by

        14       juveniles, violent crimes, are probably

        15       approximately double the national average.

        16       The numbers of homicides greatly exceed, by as

        17       much as 40 percent, the national average, and

        18       while, as I mentioned, there has been some

        19       diminution in the course of the past couple of

        20       years, I think we have to all be mindful of

        21       what we're being told by demographers and

        22       those who have looked closely at this issue.

        23       There is going to be a significant bulge,

        24       growth, perhaps as high as 25 percent, in the

        25       teen-age group, 14 to 17 years of age, when we







                                                          1877

         1       get a little bit beyond the turn of this new

         2       oncoming century.

         3                      We all know that crime is

         4       disproportionately high among teenagers and

         5       those in their early 20s, so while we can take

         6       some comfort in some reduction, the reality is

         7       that we must be very mindful of the fact that

         8       there is not only the potential but the

         9       enormous potential for yet another serious

        10       spike in juvenile crime just awaiting around

        11       the corner for us as we approach the 21st

        12       Century.

        13                      I would like to thank so many

        14       people who have been kind enough to give me

        15       their assistance in putting this bill

        16       together. Certainly the Governor is entitled

        17       to an extraordinary amount of credit for his

        18       bringing this issue to the forefront, working

        19       closely with us in our efforts to try and

        20       bring closure and, as I said a moment ago, the

        21       Assembly's interest has at long last, has at

        22       long last manifested itself in the form of a

        23       bill and hopefully this will really get us to

        24       the process where we can iron out our

        25       differences and after what has been a







                                                          1878

         1       three-year quest for me as the chairman of the

         2       Children and Families Committee, resolve this

         3       issue during this session.

         4                      Thank you, Mr. President.

         5                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

         6       Paterson.

         7                      SENATOR PATERSON:  Thank you,

         8       Mr. President, and thank you, Senator Saland

         9       for a rather informative explanation of the

        10       juvenile justice program that you are

        11       proposing, and, Mr. President, I actually

        12       didn't ask for an explanation, but I wanted

        13       one and your intuitive powers continue to

        14       amaze me.  You're serving us aptly.

        15                      If the Senator would yield to a

        16       question.

        17                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

        18       Saland, will you yield?

        19                      SENATOR SALAND:  Yes, Mr.

        20       President.

        21                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

        22       yields.

        23                      SENATOR PATERSON:  Actually,

        24       there was some aspects of the legislation I

        25       was particularly impressed with, the







                                                          1879

         1       involvement of victims in the process, which

         2       is something that for such a long time our

         3       criminal justice system has not addressed, the

         4       decision you made in the legislation to unseal

         5       the records for youthful offenders when it

         6       comes to applying for licensing for weapons,

         7       perhaps later on in their lives, the

         8       availability of that information is I think

         9       quite good and also the jurisdiction of Family

        10       Courts to issue as you have underscored in

        11       your legislation, search warrants which could

        12       be very helpful in ferreting out and

        13       preventing crime.
